--- Page 1 ---
DPS-07 Rev 2  |  Distribution Protection Standard  |  Effective 09/15/2023
Page 1
ALLENIOM UTILITIES — STANDARDS ENGINEERING
DISTRIBUTION PROTECTION STANDARD
Doc no.
Rev
Date
Owner
DPS-07
Rev 2
09/15/2023
Alleniom Standards Engineering
Effective date: 09/15/2023
Supersedes: DPS-07 Rev 1 (11/04/2019)
Classification: Engineering Standard — Distribution Protection
Approved by: Manager, Standards Engineering
1. PURPOSE
DPS-07 establishes minimum protection requirements for the interconnection of distributed energy resources
(DER) to the Alleniom Utilities distribution system. The requirements set forth herein preserve system-side fault
clearing, prevent unintentional islanding of generation onto de-energized distribution circuits, and ensure that the
utility maintains a controllable, visible interruption point at every generating facility capable of exporting power to
the distribution network.
This standard defines the equipment, functional performance, and coordination principles applicable to protective
devices installed at the point of interconnection (POI) of an export-capable DER site. It is issued by Standards
Engineering under authority of the Director of Distribution Engineering and shall be applied to all in-scope
projects at initial screening, detailed engineering review, construction, and commissioning.
2. SCOPE
This standard applies to all distribution-connected export-capable DER sites within the Alleniom Utilities service
territory, including but not limited to:
 1. Commercial small-scale DER (500 kW – 1 MW nameplate).
2. Medium-scale DER (1 MW – 5 MW nameplate).
3. Any DER of any size that is capable, by facility design or operating configuration, of exporting real power to
the distribution system through the point of common coupling.
Sub-scope DER handled under the Simplified Small-Systems Process are outside the direct application of this
standard; however, where such a facility is nonetheless configured for export, the protection principles of §4 shall
apply as adapted by the Small-Systems review.
Non-export configurations (facilities operated behind a reverse-power lockout with no export capability under any
operating condition) are outside the scope of this standard and are addressed under separate protection
guidance.
3. REFERENCES
The following documents are referenced in the application of this standard:
  IEEE 1547 — Standard for Interconnection and Interoperability of Distributed Energy Resources with
Associated Electric Power Systems Interfaces.
 IEEE C37.230 — Guide for Protective Relay Applications to Distribution Lines.
 IEEE C37.60 / IEC 62271-111 — Requirements for Overhead, Pad-Mounted, Dry-Vault, and Submersible
Automatic Circuit Reclosers.
 ANSI C57.13 — Requirements for Instrument Transformers.

--- Page 2 ---
DPS-07 Rev 2  |  Distribution Protection Standard  |  Effective 09/15/2023 Page 2
 Alleniom Utilities TCS-02 — Telemetry & Communications Standard.
 Alleniom Utilities ERP-9 — Engineering Referral Procedure.
4. PROTECTION REQUIREMENTS
4.1 General
Every distribution-connected DER site subject to this standard shall be equipped with protective equipment
sufficient to accomplish, at minimum, the following:
(a) Isolate the DER from the distribution system upon loss of the utility source, before the operation of any utility
reclosing sequence that would attempt to re-energize the affected circuit.
(b) Isolate the DER from the distribution system upon detection of abnormal voltage or frequency conditions on
the utility side of the point of interconnection, within the trip times required by the applicable interconnection
standard.
(c) Present the utility system operator with a visible, remotely operable, and lockable point of interruption
between the DER and the distribution circuit at all times when the DER is connected.
(d) Coordinate with upstream and downstream distribution protective devices such that a DER-side fault is
cleared by DER-side devices and a utility-side fault is cleared by utility-side devices, without unnecessary
tripping of either.
4.2 Point-of-Interconnection Recloser Requirement
Every export-capable in-scope DER site shall be equipped with a utility-owned point-of-interconnection
(POI) recloser. No exceptions are specified.
The POI recloser shall satisfy the following requirements:
1. Ownership and control. The POI recloser and its associated control cabinet, communications interface,
current and voltage transformers, and control power supply shall be owned, installed, maintained, and
operated by Alleniom Utilities. The DER owner shall provide the physical site, the equipment pad, primary
conductors to the recloser terminals, and any auxiliary services (grounding, station service, communications
backhaul) as specified in the site's construction package.
2. Ratings. The recloser shall be rated for the maximum continuous current, momentary current, short-circuit
interrupting current, and system voltage of the feeder or lateral to which it is connected, with margin per
Distribution Protection Engineering's feeder-specific settings sheet.
3. Functional elements. At minimum, the recloser control shall implement the following ANSI device functions,
with settings determined per site by Distribution Protection Engineering:
— 50/51 phase and 50N/51N ground overcurrent (instantaneous and time),
— 27/59 undervoltage and overvoltage,
— 81U/81O underfrequency and overfrequency,
— 25 synchronism check for closing into an energized system,
— 32 directional power element, available for use as an export-limit enforcement or reverse-power
backstop as directed by the site's engineering determination,
— 79 automatic reclosing, enabled or blocked per the coordination scheme in §5.
4. Operability. The recloser shall be capable of local manual operation, local electrical operation from the
control cabinet, and remote operation and monitoring via the utility SCADA system per TCS-02. Loss of
communications shall not defeat local protection.
Where a referenced external standard is revised, the revision in effect on the date of the site's engineering
determination shall govern, unless Standards Engineering directs otherwise in writing.
--- Page 3 ---
DPS-07 Rev 2  |  Distribution Protection Standard  |  Effective 09/15/2023
Page 3
5. Visible break and lockout. The recloser shall provide, or be paired with, a visible-break disconnect
operable by utility personnel, with provision for utility padlocking in the open position for the purpose of
clearance holds.
6. Location. The POI recloser shall be located on the utility side of the point of interconnection, at a location
accessible to Alleniom Utilities crews 24 hours per day, 7 days per week, without transiting locked customer
premises.
4.3 DER-Side Protection
DER-side protection (generator step-up transformer protection, inverter interface protection, plant collection
protection, and any owner-installed disconnects) shall be provided by the DER owner, coordinated with the POI
recloser settings, and reviewed by Alleniom Utilities Distribution Protection Engineering prior to commissioning.
DER-side protection does not substitute for the POI recloser required under §4.2.
4.4 Grounding
The DER interconnection transformer grounding configuration shall be determined per site to be compatible with
the grounding of the connected distribution circuit, in accordance with Distribution Protection Engineering's
grounding practice memorandum for the affected feeder class.
4.5 Anti-Islanding
The DER shall be equipped with anti-islanding protection meeting the trip times and non-detection zone
requirements of the applicable interconnection standard. Passive schemes based solely on utility-side voltage
and frequency measurement are permitted only where the site's system impact study demonstrates the passive
scheme's detection performance for the range of expected islanding conditions on the connected feeder;
otherwise an active or communications-assisted scheme shall be provided.
5. COORDINATION REQUIREMENTS
5.1 Coordination with Feeder Reclosing
The POI recloser shall be coordinated with the upstream feeder recloser and any mid-line reclosers such that:
 (a) The POI recloser opens on loss of the utility source before the first reclose attempt of any upstream
recloser.
(b) The POI recloser remains open and locked out until the utility source has been restored, verified stable per
the site's synchronism-check settings, and the utility system operator has authorized reconnection per the
site's operating procedure.
(c) Coordination time-current characteristics shall be documented in the site's protection coordination study
prior to energization.
5.2 Coordination with DER-Side Protection
DER-side protective devices shall clear DER-side faults without operation of the POI recloser to the extent
reasonably practicable. Where a DER-side fault is not cleared by DER-side devices within the allowable time, the
POI recloser shall trip as backup protection.
5.3 Direct Transfer Trip
Direct transfer trip (DTT) shall be applied at any site where the system impact study identifies an unacceptable
non-detection zone for anti-islanding, or where the connected feeder configuration requires supervised opening
of the POI recloser on operation of an upstream device. Where DTT is applied, the associated communications
channel shall meet the availability and monitoring requirements of TCS-02.
5.4 Reclosing Blocking
Automatic reclosing on the upstream feeder recloser may be blocked, delayed, or supervised at sites where the
DER contribution to fault current, the DER anti-islanding characteristic, or the customer load composition on the

--- Page 4 ---
DPS-07 Rev 2  |  Distribution Protection Standard  |  Effective 09/15/2023 Page 4
affected feeder warrants such a change. The determination shall be made per site by Distribution Protection
5.5 Settings Governance
All protection settings for the POI recloser, and any changes to upstream feeder recloser settings driven by the
DER interconnection, shall be issued in writing by Distribution Protection Engineering and shall not be altered in
the field without a written revision order.
6. TESTING
6.1 Factory Acceptance
The POI recloser and its control shall be subjected to factory acceptance testing per the manufacturer's standard
test protocol and per IEEE C37.60 / IEC 62271-111, with test records delivered to Alleniom Utilities prior to
shipment.
6.2 Site Acceptance
Prior to placing the DER site in service, the following site acceptance activities shall be performed and witnessed
by Alleniom Utilities:
1. Insulation resistance and dielectric withstand testing of primary and secondary circuits.
2. Current transformer and voltage transformer ratio, polarity, and burden verification.
3. Functional testing of each enabled ANSI device function against its issued setting, including pickup, timing,
and reset.
4. End-to-end trip testing from each protection element through the recloser interrupter.
5. Verification of local and remote (SCADA) control, status, and metering per TCS-02.
6. Verification of synchronism check and reclose-block logic.
7. Verification of visible-break disconnect operation and lockout provisions.
6.3 Commissioning and Cutover
Cutover of the DER site to the distribution system shall not proceed until all §6.2 activities are complete and
accepted in writing by Alleniom Utilities. The site's initial parallel operation shall be observed by the utility system
operator with the POI recloser under active SCADA supervision.
6.4 Periodic Testing
The POI recloser shall be included in the utility's periodic recloser maintenance program. DER-side protective
devices shall be tested by the DER owner on a schedule not to exceed that of comparable utility-owned
equipment, with test records made available to Alleniom Utilities on request.
6.5 Post-Event Testing
Following any operation of the POI recloser attributable to a system disturbance, a DER-side event, or a
mis-operation, Distribution Protection Engineering shall review the event records and direct such retesting or
resetting as it determines appropriate before the site is returned to service.
End of DPS-07 Rev 2 — Distribution Protection Standard. Distribution: Alleniom Standards Engineering master file;
Distribution Protection Engineering; Distribution Operations; DER Program Office; APUC filing (informational).
Engineering and recorded in the site's interconnection file.

§1   PURPOSE
This standard establishes the minimum technical and operational requirements for real-time
telemetry and communications between in-scope Distributed Energy Resource (DER) facilities
and the Alleniom Utilities System Operations Center (SOC). It governs the equipment, data
content, refresh cadence, communications transport, and cybersecurity posture required for a
DER facility to be observed and dispatchable through the utility's Supervisory Control and Data
Acquisition (SCADA) system.
TCS-02 is one component of Alleniom's DER interconnection framework. Its provisions are limited
to telemetry and communications. Requirements for interconnection classification, protective
functions, service agreements, commissioning, and other lifecycle activities are addressed in the
standards and procedures cited by the interconnection standard (DIS-01) and are outside the
scope of this document.
§2   SCOPE
TCS-02 applies to every in-scope DER site as defined by DIS-01 §3 — that is, every DER whose
nameplate capacity meets or exceeds the DER Program threshold of 500 kW. Sub-500 kW DER
handled under the Simplified Small-Systems Process is outside the scope of this standard.
TCS-02 applies to:
 a.   Commercial small-scale DER (500 kW – 1 MW).
 b.   Medium-scale DER (1 MW – 5 MW).
 c.   Aggregated DER facilities recognized as a single site under DIS-01 §3.4, where the
aggregate capacity meets or exceeds the DER Program threshold.
 d.   DER commissioned on or after the effective date of this standard, and DER
commissioned before the effective date that undergo material modification, POI relocation, or
capacity change requiring a new interconnection application.

Where a DER site interfaces with the distribution system through a shared point of common
coupling with other generation, the aggregate facility is the object of this standard, and the
aggregate is measured and controlled as a single interconnected entity.
§3   RTU REQUIREMENTS
§3.1   Ownership and installation
Each in-scope DER site shall be equipped with a utility-owned Remote Terminal Unit (RTU)
installed at, or immediately adjacent to, the point of interconnection. The RTU shall be procured,
owned, installed, configured, maintained, and — where required — replaced by Alleniom Utilities.
The customer shall provide the physical mounting location, environmental enclosure, station AC
service, and communications entrance conduit specified in the utility's site-specific RTU
installation drawing.
§3.3   Functional requirements
Each RTU shall, at minimum:
 a.   Poll the DER facility's generation metering, inverter/PCS gateway, and station
instrumentation at the refresh cadence specified in §6.
 b.   Encode and forward the required data points (§6) to the Alleniom SCADA front-end
processors over an approved communications path (§4).
 c.   Timestamp all values to a common reference (§3.5) and buffer data locally for a minimum
of seventy-two (72) hours in the event of communications loss, with automatic backfill upon
restoration.
 d.   Report communications status, device health, and configuration version to SCADA as
diagnostic points.
 e.   Accept authenticated remote configuration updates and firmware from Alleniom
SCADA/EMS Engineering only.
§3.4   Environmental and station-service requirements
The RTU enclosure shall meet the environmental rating specified in the site-specific installation
drawing. Station AC service to the enclosure shall be provided by the customer through a
dedicated branch circuit backed by an uninterruptible supply sized for a minimum four (4) hour
outage ride-through, sufficient to maintain telemetry through short-duration station outages.
§3.5   Time synchronization
The RTU shall discipline its internal clock to an authoritative time source using either GNSS (GPS)
time or the Alleniom SCADA network time reference. All values reported to SCADA shall carry a
timestamp accurate to within ±1 second of UTC.
§3.6   Commissioning and end-to-end verification
§3.2   Approved models
The utility-owned RTU shall be one of the three models currently used for utility-owned RTU
service: YOT-8963, YOT-8856, or YOT-7963. Substitution is not permitted. A customer power
plant controller (PPC) may use any RTU on the plant side, provided it can communicate with the
utility-owned RTU via DNP3 (§4.2).

Analog values shall be updated to SCADA at intervals no longer than four (4) seconds using DNP3
Class 1/2 event reporting for point-on-change and Class 0 integrity poll no less frequently than
every sixty (60) seconds. Status points shall be reported by exception on change of state, with an
integrity poll no less frequently than every sixty (60) seconds. Cumulative energy registers shall be
reported no less frequently than every five (5) minutes.
§6.3   Data quality
Every value delivered to SCADA shall carry a DNP3 quality flag. Values shall be marked online,
restart, communications lost, or over-range as circumstances warrant. Values held constant by the
RTU during communications loss shall not be reported as online upon restoration; they shall be
reported with the communications-lost flag until fresh source values are acquired.
§6.4   Retention
Alleniom retains all telemetry from in-scope DER sites in the historian for a minimum of thirty-six
(36) months at the raw acquisition cadence, and indefinitely at hourly aggregation, for planning,
engineering analysis, and regulatory reporting.
§7   CYBERSECURITY
§7.1   Applicability
The RTU, the communications transport between the RTU and Alleniom SCADA, and any
customer equipment that shares a physical or logical interface with the RTU are subject to this
section. Alleniom-owned assets covered here are administered under Alleniom's cyber-security
program consistent with NIST SP 800-82 and NERC CIP where applicable.
§7.2   Access control
Local and remote access to the RTU is limited to Alleniom SCADA/EMS Engineering and to
Alleniom-authorized service personnel. Local craft access requires two-factor authentication
against Alleniom's identity system. Passwords, shared secrets, and cryptographic keys are
managed by Alleniom and are not disclosed to the customer, developer, or any third party.
§7.3   Communications security
DNP3 Secure Authentication v5 shall be enabled where supported by the RTU. All
communications traversing any non-utility segment shall be tunneled through an
Alleniom-managed VPN using IPsec (IKEv2) with mutual certificate authentication. Certificates
shall have a maximum validity of thirteen (13) months and are rotated by Alleniom.
§7.4   Firmware, configuration, and change management
RTU firmware and configuration are updated only by Alleniom SCADA/EMS Engineering, following
the Alleniom change-management process. Firmware images shall be verified against a
cryptographic signature prior to installation. The customer shall not attempt to modify, upgrade, or
reconfigure the RTU or the utility-owned communications equipment.
§7.5   Logging and monitoring
The RTU shall log authentication events, configuration changes, communications state transitions,
and firmware operations. Logs are forwarded to Alleniom's centralized log-management system.
Anomalies detected by that system are handled per Alleniom's cyber-security incident response
procedure.

Distribution Protection Engineering
Site: Prairie Corridor Business Park PV (PXA-2024-0343), POI recloser PC-POI-R1 with control NPC-38.
Issued for the site acceptance at cutover under DPS-07 §6.2, against settings sheet DPE-PC-POI-R1 Rev A.
To be performed after installation and witnessed by Alleniom Utilities; results recorded on this form at the test.
Steps
Step 1 Insulation and dielectric. Measure insulation resistance of primary and secondary circuits at 5 kV DC for
one minute; apply the manufacturer's dielectric withstand test to the secondary wiring. Record the values.
Step 2 Instrument transformers. Verify CT ratio 200:5, polarity and burden; verify VT ratio 7200:120 V and
polarity on both sides of the interrupter.
Step 3 Functional testing. Test the elements below against settings sheet Rev A by secondary injection: pickup,
timing and reset for each. Elements: 50/51, 50N/51N, 27, 59, 81U, 81O, 32; 25 and 79 under step 6.
Step 4 End-to-end trip. From each element of step 3, trip the recloser through the interrupter and confirm the
open indication locally and at SCADA.
Step 5 Control, status and metering. Operate the recloser locally and from SCADA; confirm status points and
metering at the SCADA operator display against the RTU point table SCADA-PC-RTU-CFG-01.
Step 6 Synchronism check and reclose logic. With the utility source live and the park bus dead, confirm the 25
element permits the close; close from the control cabinet and confirm the recloser closes. Open the recloser,
open the upstream line disconnect to de-energize the line side, and confirm a close command is refused. Trip
the recloser by secondary injection on the 27 element and confirm it goes to lockout with 79 blocked; confirm
the lockout holds until the operator release. Restore the line side, wait the stable-source time of settings sheet
Rev A (5 minutes), release, and confirm the close through 25.
Step 7 Visible break. Operate the visible-break disconnect; apply the utility padlock in the open position and
confirm the clearance hold.
Acceptance
Accepted in writing by Distribution Protection Engineering on completion of steps 1 to 7 (DPS-07 §6.3).
Prepared: Nolan Achterberg, P.E., Distribution Protection Engineer, 07/09/2025.

P11 [Normal]: SUBJECT: DER Backlog Review — Program Manager Tasking
P13 [Normal]: 1. Confirmation of directive
P14 [Normal]: This memorandum confirms and operationalizes the internal directive issued 06/27/2025 by Dana Whitcomb, Vice President, Distribution Operations (DIR-2025-0627), ordering a full backlog review of the commercial DER interconnection program. Regulatory Affairs accepts ownership of the external commitments arising from that directive and, by this memorandum, assigns the internal queue-cleanup work to the DER Program Manager.
P15 [Normal]: The scope of the backlog review, as established by the VP, is the entire active, on-hold, and past-study-timeline population of the commercial DER program queue as of the anchor date. Every application is to be accounted for by name, application number, current posture, and next required action. Nothing in this memorandum reduces, expands, or alters that scope.
P16 [Normal]: 2. Governing deadlines
P17 [Normal]: Two dates fix the outer boundary of this work and are not to be revisited without written concurrence from the VP office and Regulatory Affairs:
P18 [List Bullet]: 08/15/2025 — Response to the Alleron Municipal League. Regulatory Affairs will issue the formal written response to the League's 06/20/2025 letter. The response will be substantive and project-specific, addressing the League's five enumerated requests on behalf of the fourteen member municipalities and school districts. Regulatory Affairs is the signatory; the DER Program Manager is responsible for delivering the underlying queue accounting on which the response will rest.
P19 [List Bullet]: 09/10/2025 — APUC briefing. The queue accounting must be complete and defensible in advance of the briefing to the Alleron Public Utilities Commission's Energy Resources Division. Regulatory Affairs will not present partial data to the Commission. Any application whose disposition remains open on 09/10/2025 must have a written reason on file, not an oral one.
P20 [Normal]: Any interim regulatory information request the Division may issue in advance of the briefing will be answered from the same underlying record and will not create a separate work product for the Program Manager beyond timely disposition of the affected applications.
P21 [Normal]: 3. Tasking of the DER Program Manager
P22 [Normal]: The DER Program Manager is tasked, effective immediately, with producing the following queue-cleanup inputs. [body.p.3]: **TO:        [size=10.5]**Lena Kovalchuk, SOC Shift Supervisor, System Operations Center (lena.kovalchuk@alleniom.com)[size=10.5]

Rennick, Commissioning Coordinator, DER Program Office; Marcus Deele, Lead SCADA/Telemetry Engineer, SCADA/EMS Engineering; Nolan Achterberg, P.E., Distribution Protection Engineer; Evan Solberg, Standards Engineer; Dana Whitcomb, Vice President, Distribution Operations[size=10.5]
[body.p.6]: **DATE:      [size=10.5]**07/14/2025[size=10.5]
[body.p.7]: **SUBJECT:   [size=10.5]**Corwyn Office Complex PV (Application PXA-2023-0629, 700 kW ac, Feeder ALN-072) — Engineering Review of Record for Requested 08/04/2025 Permission to Operate[size=10.5]
[body.p.8] (style=Heading 1): **1. Executive Determination[color=#1B365D,size=11.5]**
[body.p.9]: On 07/10/2025, Corwyn Realty Partners (Nadia Ferreira-Holt, Director of Property Operations) submitted a written request for Permission to Operate (PTO) for the 700 kW (ac) Corwyn Office Complex PV facility (Application PXA-2023-0629, 2400 Corwyn Parkway, Wrenford, Alleron 04WR, Feeder ALN-072) effective 08/04/2025. Working from the interconnection and commissioning record as it stands at 07/14/2025, the DER Program Office has completed its engineering review of all matters within its scope. Our determination is as follows:[size=10.5]
[body.p.10] (style=List Bullet): **Determination on the Record as of 07/14/2025 — HOLD: **Permission to Operate CANNOT issue on the record as it stands at 07/14/2025. The System Operations Center (SOC) must HOLD PTO until the standing station-service, inverter control-power/telemetry, and SCADA polling/confirmation items identified in Section 3 are resolved on the record.
[body.p.11] (style=List Bullet): **Determination for 08/04/2025 — CONDITIONAL (Achievable Before 08/04/2025): **Permission to Operate CAN issue on the requested date of 08/04/2025 IF AND ONLY IF those standing items are settled and verified prior to issuance on 08/04/2025 — and YES, all required corrective actions CAN be completed before 08/04/2025 within the 21 calendar days (15 business days) remaining between 07/14/2025 and 08/04/2025. Conversely, if any of the items in Section 3 remains unsettled on 08/04/2025, the SOC must hold PTO.
[body.p.12]: Specifically, while the Executed Interconnection Service Agreement (ISA-Corwyn-Office-Complex, effective 09/12/2024), the City of Wrenford final electrical inspection approval (Permit WEP-25-0317, approved 07/02/2025), the Vexlar Energy Certificate of Conformance (VX-CC-25-0522, 05/22/2025), the Certified Equipment List check (CEL-2025-Q2), the on-site witness test record (WT-0629-01, passed 07/08/2025), primary revenue metering (RM-0629, set and tested 07/08/2025), and the PV array/canopy NFPA 70 (NEC 2023) design calculations all check out satisfactorily, the as-built equipment and communications schedules (Drawings E-101 Rev C and E-401 Rev C, 06/24/2025) contain an interlocking station-service and telemetry defect that prevents live telemetry at the SOC while the POI recloser is kept open before PTO:[size=10.5]
[body.p.13] (style=List Bullet): **1. Utility RTU Station AC Service Fed Downstream of the Open POI Recloser (Drawing E-101 Rev C; ISA §§5.2, 6.1, 6.2, 7.2, 8.3–8.5; TCS-02 §§3.4, 4.3, 5; DPS-07 Rev 2 §§4.1(c), 4.2(4), 5.1(b), 6.3): **Under Drawing E-101 Rev C (Equipment Schedule, rows 4–6), auxiliary panel PP-1 (which supplies Circuit 1, the dedicated 20 A, 120 V station AC service to the utility RTU enclosure on the POI pole through its 1.5 kVA online UPS rated for 5.5 h at the RTU load, and Circuit 2, the 20 A SWBD-PV enclosure heaters) is fed from auxiliary transformer TX-1 (15 kVA, 480 V to 120/240 V), which is fed from a 40 A two-pole breaker in PV switchboard SWBD-PV on the customer/DER side of step-up transformer T-1, primary switch PSW-1, and the Company's POI recloser. Under ISA §6.1, the POI recloser is kept open at all times before PTO except during the witness test (and was opened by Distribution Operations at 15:35 on 07/08/2025 at the conclusion of Witness Test WT-0629-01). With the POI recloser open, T-1, SWBD-PV, TX-1, and PP-1 are completely de-energized; 5.5 hours after 15:35 on 07/08/2025, the RTU's UPS battery depleted and the utility RTU lost power and telemetry.
[body.p.14] (style=List Bullet): **2. Inverter Internal Control Power Derived from De-Energized 480 V AC Terminals Before PTO (Drawing E-101 Rev C row 7; Drawing E-401 Rev C; ISA §§6.1, 6.2, 7.2, 12.1; TCS-02 §§5(c), 6.1, 6.3): **Under Drawing E-101 Rev C (row 7), each Vexlar VX-140C inverter (INV-C1 to INV-C5) derives its internal control power "from the inverter's own ac output terminals." Under Drawing E-401 Rev C (Monitoring and Communications Schedule, Links row 7), the utility RTU polls INV-C1 to INV-C5 over COM-RTU (RS-485 port 2, multi-drop bus) for per-inverter AC power and status required by TCS-02 §6.1. Even after the RTU enclosure itself is re-fed from independent building house power, while the POI recloser is kept open before PTO under ISA §6.1 (which contains no pre-PTO backfeed clause), SWBD-PV and the inverter 480 V AC terminals remain de-energized, leaving the inverters without AC control power to communicate over COM-RTU and causing the RTU to flag per-inverter points as communications-lost (bad quality) under TCS-02 §6.3, barring PTO under TCS-02 §5(c).
[body.p.15] (style=List Bullet): **3. Per-Inverter SCADA Polling Cadence on Drawing E-401 Rev C and Day-of-PTO Live-Telemetry Re-Confirmation (Drawing E-401 Rev C; CX-CW-01; TCS-02 §§3.3(a), 5(b)–(c), 6.1, 6.2; ISA §§6.2, 6.3, 7.2; DPS-07 §6.3): **Drawing E-401 Rev C (Points sheet, row 2) lists a "5 min" interval for "AC power, energy, voltage and current per inverter" from INV-C1 to INV-C5 and "On change" for inverter status/fault codes without distinguishing customer cabinet DAS-1 from the utility RTU link COM-RTU, whereas TCS-02 §§6.1–6.2 require analog Gross generation (per inverter block) (kW) at SCADA at ≤ 4-second intervals (with ≤ 60-second Class 0 integrity poll) and status points on change with ≤ 60-second integrity poll. In addition, the SOC live-telemetry sign-off on Commissioning Checklist CX-CW-01 was recorded on 07/08/2025 (during the witness-test switching window, two days before the 07/10/2025 PTO request), whereas TCS-02 §5(c) requires all §6 points to be valid at the SCADA operator display at the moment PTO is issued.

Company RTU and POI Recloser Installation, Configuration, and Commissioning Tests: **The installation, configuration, and commissioning tests of the Company's utility-owned RTU and POI recloser at the site (under separate review by SCADA/EMS Engineering — Marcus Deele, and Distribution Protection Engineering — Nolan Achterberg, P.E.; recorded on CX-CW-01 as accepted on 07/08/2025 under TCS-02 §3.6 and DPS-07 §6.2).
[body.p.20] (style=List Bullet): **2. POI Recloser Settings and Protection Coordination Study: **The POI recloser's settings and the protection coordination study behind them (issued on 06/18/2025 by Distribution Protection Engineering — Nolan Achterberg, P.E., under DPS-07 §5.1, and kept outside these records).
[body.p.21] (style=List Bullet): **3. Queue Position: **The site's queue position (under separate review by Meera Vellanki, Manager, Interconnection Studies, under the weekly queue reports; carried in 2025-07-14_Active_Queue_Report.xlsx at row 18 as active in commissioning status with application date 07/11/2023).
[body.p.22] (style=List Bullet): **4. System Impact Study and Conditions: **The system impact study and its conditions (under separate review by Ivo Grantham's DER Planning Group, which keeps them outside these records).
[body.p.23]: Nothing else is under separate review. All other contractual, technical, code, equipment, witness-test, metering, and customer-side telemetry/station-service provisions on the record as of 07/14/2025 have been reviewed for this memorandum under ISA-Corwyn-Office-Complex §2.1, which incorporates the Tariff (§12), Alleniom DER Interconnection Standard DIS-01 Rev 4 (effective 03/01/2024), Alleniom Distribution Protection Standard DPS-07 Rev 2 (effective 09/15/2023), Alleniom Telemetry & Communications Standard TCS-02 (Rev 1, effective 06/01/2021), Alleniom Witness Test & Waiver Procedure ENG-PRC-014 Rev 3 (effective 01/15/2025) and Certified Equipment List CEL-2025-Q2 (published 04/30/2025), IEEE 1547-2018, IEEE 1547.1-2020, and NFPA 70 (National Electrical Code), 2023 edition.[size=10.5]
[body.p.24] (style=Heading 1): **3. Matters on the Record Standing in the Way of Permission to Operate[color=#1B365D,size=11.5]**
[body.p.25] (style=Heading 2): **3.1 Obstacle 1: Utility RTU Station AC Service (PP-1 Circuit 1 / TX-1) and SWBD-PV Enclosure Heaters (PP-1 Circuit 2) Are Fed from SWBD-PV on the Customer/DER Side of the POI Recloser[color=#1B365D,size=10.5]**
[body.p.26]: **What it is: [size=10.5]**In PXA-2023-0629_Corwyn_Equipment_Schedule.xlsx (Drawing E-101 Rev C, prepared by K. Osei, Brantley Electric Company, 06/24/2025, rows 2–6), the customer's station AC service to the utility RTU enclosure on the POI pole is wired as follows: (a) PV switchboard SWBD-PV (480Y/277 V, 3-phase, 4-wire, 1,200 A bus, 1,200 A main breaker) contains five 225 A inverter breakers (INV-C1 to INV-C5) and a 40 A two-pole breaker feeding auxiliary transformer TX-1 (15 kVA, single-phase, 480 V to 120/240 V); (b) TX-1 feeds auxiliary panel PP-1 (120/240 V, single-phase, 3-wire, 100 A bus, 70 A main breaker); and (c) PP-1 Circuit 1 is the dedicated 20 A, 120 V branch circuit (2 × 12 AWG Cu and 12 AWG Cu ground in 3/4 in. Schedule 40 PVC at 600 mm cover to the POI pole, then 3/4 in. rigid steel conduit up the pole) supplying the utility RTU enclosure through the 1.5 kVA online UPS in that enclosure (rated for 5.5 hours of ride-through at the RTU load), while PP-1 Circuit 2 (20 A) supplies the SWBD-PV enclosure heaters. However, SWBD-PV is connected to Feeder ALN-072 (13.2 kV) through step-up transformer T-1 (750 kVA, 13.2 kV grounded wye to 480Y/277 V) and primary switch PSW-1 (15 kV, 200 A load-break with 65E fuses) on the customer/DER side (downstream) of the Company's POI recloser on the north-lot pole (ISA-Corwyn-Office-Complex Exhibit A, Exhibit B §B.2). Whenever the POI recloser is open (or whenever PSW-1 or the SWBD-PV 1,200 A main breaker is open), T-1, SWBD-PV, TX-1, and PP-1 have no AC source (the five Vexlar VX-140C inverters are UL 1741-SB grid-following utility-interactive inverters that cease to energize within 2.0 s when the POI recloser opens and cannot energize a dead bus). Once PP-1 loses AC voltage, the 1.5 kVA online UPS in the RTU enclosure runs on battery for 5.5 hours (Equipment Schedule row 6; Corvane OL-1500R UPS Data Sheet) and then shuts down completely, cutting off all power to the utility RTU.[size=10.5]
[body.p.27]: **Operational Effect Pre-PTO and Post-PTO: [size=10.5]**During the witness test on 07/08/2025, Distribution Operations closed the POI recloser locally at 08:10 under switching order DO-2025-0677 and opened it locally at 15:35 (Witness Test Record WT-0629-01, p. 1). While the POI recloser was closed during that 7-hour 25-minute test window, Feeder ALN-072 energized T-1, SWBD-PV, TX-1, and PP-1, so the RTU had AC station service and SCADA/EMS Engineering (Marcus Deele) and the SOC Shift Supervisor (Lena Kovalchuk) observed valid points and recorded live telemetry on 07/08/2025 (Commissioning Checklist CX-CW-01, pp. 1–2). Once Distribution Operations opened the POI recloser at 15:35 on 07/08/2025 as required by ISA §6.1 ("At all other times before permission to operate the POI recloser is kept open"), PP-1 lost AC power; 5.5 hours later (approximately 21:05 on 07/08/2025), the RTU UPS depleted and the RTU went dead. Thus, while the POI recloser remains open awaiting PTO, the RTU has no station service and cannot provide live telemetry. Furthermore, even after PTO, any time the POI recloser trips and locks out on a feeder fault awaiting SOC operator authorization to reconnect (DPS-07 §5.1(b); ISA §8.4), is opened by the Company (ISA §8.3), or any time PSW-1 or the SWBD-PV main breaker is opened for a clearance (ISA §8.5), the RTU will lose AC station service and die after 5.5 hours even though utility feeder power and office-building power remain available — blinding the SOC to POI recloser status and analog points and defeating remote SCADA operation of the POI recloser. (In addition, PP-1 Circuit 2 feeding the SWBD-PV anti-condensation enclosure heaters is de-energized whenever SWBD-PV is de-energized, which is precisely when space heating is needed outdoors.)[size=10.5]
[body.p.28]: **What it rests on: [size=10.5]**(1) ISA-Corwyn-Office-Complex §4.1 (design, construction, commissioning, and operation in conformity with DIS-01 Rev 4, DPS-07 Rev 2, and TCS-02), §5.2 (Interconnection Customer provides and maintains station service for the Company's RTU), §6.1 ("Before permission to operate, the Company may place the Facility in parallel with its distribution system solely for the witness test of the Facility... At all other times before permission to operate the POI recloser is kept open"), §6.2 ("Parallel operation begins only with the Company's written permission to operate, issued once... telemetry is live at the System Operations Center"), §6.3 (first parallel operation observed by SOC with POI recloser under SCADA supervision), §7.2 (customer provides RTU provisions per TCS-02 §5; live telemetry at the SOC is a condition of PTO), §§8.3–8.5 (Company disconnection, SOC reconnection release, and clearances), and Exhibits A & B; (2) TCS-02 §3.1 & §3.4 ("Station AC service to the enclosure shall be provided by the customer through a dedicated branch circuit backed by an uninterruptible supply sized for a minimum four (4) hour outage ride-through, sufficient to maintain telemetry through short-duration station outages"), §4.3 (≥ 99.5% monthly telemetry availability; persistent loss of telemetry constitutes a departure from the site's interconnection basis), and §5(a)–(c) (no PTO without live telemetry presenting all required §6 points as valid at the SCADA operator display at the moment PTO is issued); (3) DIS-01 Rev 4 §5 Table 5-1 (Category 2) and §6 (live telemetry per TCS-02 §5 required as a condition of PTO); (4) DPS-07 Rev 2 §4.1(c), §4.2 item 4 (remote operation and monitoring of the POI recloser via utility SCADA per TCS-02), §5.1(b) (recloser lockout until utility source is verified stable and utility system operator authorizes reconnection), and §6.3 (active SCADA supervision during cutover/initial parallel operation); and (5) Drawing E-101 Rev C (rows 2–6), Drawing E-401 Rev C (Cabinet row 2, showing independent building house power at office building panel LP-2 in the parking structure electrical room), Witness Test Record WT-0629-01 (p. 1), and Certificate of Final Approval WEP-25-0317 (07/02/2025).[size=10.5]
[body.p.29]: **What has to be done about it and by whom: [size=10.5]**Corwyn Realty Partners (Nadia Ferreira-Holt) and its electrical contractor Brantley Electric Company (K. Osei, Lic. #EC-12306) must re-feed the utility RTU station AC service (either the dedicated 20 A, 120 V branch circuit to the POI pole RTU enclosure UPS, or auxiliary panel PP-1 / TX-1 so that both PP-1 Circuit 1 for the RTU UPS and PP-1 Circuit 2 for the SWBD-PV enclosure heaters remain continuously energized when the POI recloser, PSW-1, or SWBD-PV main is open) from a continuously energized, unswitched building house-power panel on the Corwyn Office Complex load service (such as office building panel LP-2 in the ground-floor electrical room of the parking structure, which already supplies a 20 A, 120 V circuit to monitoring cabinet DAS-1 per Drawing E-401 Rev C, Cabinet row 2). I have repaired `/filesystem/Corwyn_PTO_Memo.docx` and re-verified consistency across all canonical entries in `/tmp/.ple_work_b5121503ed29/facts.json`, `/filesystem/Corwyn_PTO_Memo.docx`, and OpenProject Work Package **`#47`**.

---

### Deliverables Produced
1. **Engineering Review Memorandum (Word Document)**: `/filesystem/Corwyn_PTO_Memo.docx`
   - **To**: Lena Kovalchuk, SOC Shift Supervisor, System Operations Center (`lena.kovalchuk@alleniom.com`)
   - **From**: Reviewing Engineer, P.E., DER Program Office (Tomás Ibarra, P.E., Senior Interconnection Engineer)
   - **Date**: `07/14/2025`
2. **OpenProject Work Package**: Work Package **`#47`** (`Resolve Corwyn Office Complex PV (PXA-2023-0629) pre-PTO station-service and telemetry hold for 08/04/2025 PTO`) in project **DER Program Backlog Review** (`project_id: 3`, assigned to Commissioning Coordinator `S. Rennick`, start date `2025-07-14`, due date `2025-08-04`, priority `High`, with watchers `Lena Kovalchuk`, `Tomás Ibarra`, `Marcus Deele`, and `K. Ondras`).

---

### Key Results & Determination

#### 1. Determination on Permission to Operate (`08/04/2025`)
* **On the Record as It Stands at `07/14/2025` — HOLD:** Permission to Operate **cannot issue** on the as-built record as it stands at `07/14/2025`. The System Operations Center must **hold** PTO and keep the POI recloser on Feeder `ALN-072 (13.2 kV, three-phase)` open (`ISA-Corwyn-Office-Complex §6.1`) until the standing station-service and telemetry obstacles summarized below are settled.
* **For the Requested Date of `08/04/2025` — CONDITIONAL (Achievable Before `08/04/2025`):** Permission to Operate **can issue on `08/04/2025`** if and only if the standing items below are settled and verified prior to issuance on `08/04/2025`. **All required corrective actions can be completed before `08/04/2025`** within the 21 calendar days (15 business days) available between `07/14/2025` and `08/04/2025`, because all utility-owned equipment (POI recloser, utility RTU, and primary revenue meter `RM-0629`) is already installed and tested on site, and an unswitched 120 V building house-power source (`office building panel LP-2` in the ground-floor electrical room of the parking structure) and underground conduit routes are already in place.

---

#### 2. Matters on the Record Standing in the Way of Permission to Operate

1. **Obstacle 1 — Utility RTU Station AC Service (`PP-1 Circuit 1`) and `SWBD-PV` Enclosure Heaters (`PP-1 Circuit 2`) Fed from `SWBD-PV` on the Customer/DER Side of the Open POI Recloser**
   * **What it is:** Under `PXA-2023-0629_Corwyn_Equipment_Schedule.xlsx` (`Drawing E-101 Rev C`, `06/24/2025`, rows 2–6), auxiliary panel `PP-1` (`120/240 V`, `100 A` bus, `70 A` main breaker) supplies **`Circuit 1`** (the dedicated `20 A`, `120 V` circuit to the utility RTU enclosure on the POI pole through its `1.5 kVA` online UPS rated for `5.5 h` at the RTU load) and **`Circuit 2`** (`20 A` `SWBD-PV` enclosure heaters). However, `PP-1` is fed by auxiliary transformer `TX-1` (`15 kVA`, `480 V to 120/240 V`), which is fed from a `40 A` two-pole breaker in `SWBD-PV` (`480Y/277 V`) on the customer/DER side of step-up transformer `T-1` (`750 kVA`), primary switch `PSW-1`, and the Company's POI recloser. During the witness test on `07/08/2025`, Distribution Operations closed the POI recloser locally at `08:10` under switching order `DO-2025-0677`, energizing `T-1`, `SWBD-PV`, `TX-1`, and `PP-1`, and opened it locally at `15:35` (`WT-0629-01`, p. 1). Because `ISA §6.1` mandates that *"At all other times before permission to operate the POI recloser is kept open,"* `PP-1` lost AC power at `15:35` on `07/08/2025`, the `5.5 h` RTU UPS battery depleted around `21:05` on `07/08/2025`, and the utility RTU lost power and SCADA telemetry. Post-PTO, any trip/lockout of the POI recloser (`DPS-07 §5.1(b)`, `ISA §8.4`), Company opening (`ISA §8.3`), or clearance opening of `PSW-1` or `SWBD-PV` main (`ISA §8.5`) would similarly de-energize `PP-1`, shutting down the RTU after 5.5 hours (and de-energizing the `SWBD-PV` space heaters while `SWBD-PV` is cold).
   * **What it rests on:** `Drawing E-101 Rev C` (rows 2–6); `Drawing E-401 Rev C` (`Cabinet` row 2); `WT-0629-01` (p. 1); `ISA-Corwyn-Office-Complex §§4.1, 5.2, 6.1, 6.2, 6.3, 7.2, 8.3–8.5, Exhibits A & B`; `TCS-02 §§3.1, 3.4, 4.3, 5(a)–(c)`; `DIS-01 Rev 4 §5 Table 5-1 & §6`; `DPS-07 Rev 2 §§4.1(c), 4.2(4), 5.1(b), 6.3`.
   * **What has to be done and by whom:** **Corwyn Realty Partners** (`Nadia Ferreira-Holt, Director of Property Operations`) and **Brantley Electric Company (Alleron Electrical Contractor Lic. #EC-12306)** (`K. Osei, Electrical Engineer`) must re-feed the utility RTU station AC service (or `PP-1` / `TX-1` so both `PP-1 Circuit 1` and `PP-1 Circuit 2` remain energized when `SWBD-PV` is de-energized) from an unswitched, continuously energized building house-power panel on the office-complex load service (such as `office building panel LP-2` in the parking-structure electrical room, which already feeds `DAS-1` on circuit 14 per `Drawing E-401 Rev C`), issue revised `Drawing E-101 Rev D`, and obtain supplemental electrical inspection approval from the **City of Wrenford Department of Inspections** (`Dolores Achebe, Chief Electrical Inspector`) under Permit `WEP-25-0317` (`ISA §§4.2, 6.2`).
   * **Can it be done before `08/04/2025`?** **Yes** (within the 21 calendar days / 15 business days available).

2. **Obstacle 2 — Inverter Internal Control Power (`INV-C1` to `INV-C5`) Derived from 480 V AC Output Terminals While the POI Recloser Is Kept Open Before PTO (`COM-RTU` Telemetry Deadlock)**
   * **What it is:** Under `Drawing E-401 Rev C` (`Links` row 7), the utility RTU polls `INV-C1` to `INV-C5` over `COM-RTU` (`RS-485 port 2, one multi-drop bus`) for per-inverter AC power (`Gross generation (per inverter block)`) and status (`Inverter/PCS block status`) required by `TCS-02 §6.1`. Under `Drawing E-101 Rev C` (row 7), each of the `5 x Vexlar Energy VX-140C (140 kW ac, 480 V, 3-phase, UL 1741-SB, firmware family 4.2, build 4.2.7)` inverters takes its `"control power internal, from the inverter's own ac output terminals."` Even after the RTU enclosure is re-fed from building house power, while the POI recloser is kept open before PTO under `ISA §6.1` (which contains no pre-PTO backfeed provision, unlike `ISA-Halbray-Field-Site-3`), `T-1` and `SWBD-PV` are de-energized, leaving `INV-C1` to `INV-C5` without 480 V AC at their output terminals to power their internal control/RS-485 electronics. Under `TCS-02 §6.3`, the RTU must report those unreachable per-inverter points with the `communications-lost` quality flag, preventing satisfaction of `TCS-02 §5(c)` (which requires all `§6` points to be valid and not flagged bad-quality at the SCADA operator display at the moment PTO is issued).
   * **What it rests on:** `Drawing E-101 Rev C` (row 7); `Drawing E-401 Rev C` (`Links` row 7); `ISA-Corwyn-Office-Complex §§6.1, 6.2, 7.2, 12.1`; `TCS-02 §§3.3(a), 5(c), 6.1, 6.3`.
   * **What has to be done and by whom:** Either **(Path A)** **Corwyn Realty Partners** (`Nadia Ferreira-Holt`) and **Alleniom Utilities** (`Dana Whitcomb, VP Distribution Operations`, coordinated by the **DER Program Office** — `K. Ondras` / `S. Rennick, Commissioning, DER Program Office`) execute a brief written change order under `ISA §12.1` authorizing pre-PTO backfeed of `T-1` and `SWBD-PV` under a **Distribution Operations** switching order (with `INV-C1` to `INV-C5` disabled from parallel export / in standby) so 480 V AC energizes inverter control power and `COM-RTU` reports valid standby status and `0 kW` output prior to PTO issuance; **or (Path B)** **Corwyn Realty Partners** and **Brantley Electric Company** (`K. Osei`), with **Vexlar Energy** (`T. Lindgren`), supply continuous auxiliary control power from house power to the inverters' communications cards so `COM-RTU` stays online while `SWBD-PV` is open.
   * **Can it be done before `08/04/2025`?** **Yes.**

3. **Obstacle 3 — Per-Inverter SCADA Polling Cadence on `Drawing E-401 Rev C` (`5 min` vs. `TCS-02 §6.2` `≤ 4 s` Cadence), `Drawing E-301` Schedule Clarification, and Fresh Day-of-PTO SOC Live-Telemetry Confirmation (`TCS-02 §5(c)`)**
   * **What it is:** (a) `Drawing E-401 Rev C` (`Header` and `Points` rows 2–3) covers both `DAS-1` and `COM-RTU` (`ISA §7.2`) but lists a `"5 min"` interval for `"AC power, energy, voltage and current per inverter"` and `"On change"` for `"Inverter status and fault codes"`, whereas `TCS-02 §§6.1–6.2` require analog `Gross generation (per inverter block) (kW)` to update to SCADA at **`≤ 4 s`** intervals (with a `≤ 60 s` Class 0 integrity poll) and status points to report on change with a **`≤ 60 s`** integrity poll (`5 min` applies only to cumulative energy registers `kWh` and customer historian `DAS-1`). (b) `Drawing E-301 Rev C` (`PV Output Circuits` row 2) should explicitly clarify `"in individual 2 in. rigid steel conduits (one per combiner)"` down the inverter column to match the plural `"Column risers"` in `Drawing E-201 Rev C` and the un-derated `236.6 A` ampacity (`NEC Ch. 9 Table 1` & `310.15(C)(1)`). (c) The SOC live-telemetry sign-off on Commissioning Checklist `CX-CW-01 Rev 2 (07/14/2025)` was recorded on `07/08/2025` during the witness-test switching window (`08:10 to 15:35`, two days before the `07/10/2025` PTO request and before the POI recloser opened at `15:35`), whereas `TCS-02 §5(c)` requires live telemetry presenting all `§6` points as valid **at the moment PTO is issued**.
   * **What it rests on:** `Drawing E-401 Rev C`; `Drawing E-301 Rev C`; `CX-CW-01 Rev 2 (07/14/2025)`; `TCS-02 §§3.3(a), 5(b)–(c), 6.1, 6.2`; `ISA §§6.2, 6.3, 7.2`; `DPS-07 §6.3`.
   * **What has to be done and by whom:** **Corwyn Realty Partners** and **Brantley Electric Company** (`K. Osei`) issue `Drawing E-401 Rev D` (and `Drawing E-301 Rev D` clarification) and confirm with **SCADA/EMS Engineering** (`Marcus Deele`) that `COM-RTU` (`RS-485 port 2`) updates at the `TCS-02 §6.2` cadence (`≤ 4 s` analog / `≤ 60 s` integrity poll); once Obstacles 1 and 2 are resolved, **SCADA/EMS Engineering** (`Marcus Deele`) verifies all `TCS-02 §6` points valid at SCADA, **Commissioning Coordinator** (`S. Rennick, Commissioning, DER Program Office`) updates `CX-CW-01`, and the **SOC Shift Supervisor** (`Lena Kovalchuk`) confirms live telemetry at the moment PTO issues on `08/04/2025` (`TCS-02 §5(c)`) and observes first parallel operation under active SCADA supervision (`ISA §6.3`, `DPS-07 §6.3`).
   * **Can it be done before `08/04/2025`?** **Yes.**

---

#### 3. Basis of Review for All Other Record Items & Carve-Out of the Four Matters Under Separate Review
* **Verified Compliant on the Record at `07/14/2025`:** Executed `ISA-Corwyn-Office-Complex` (`09/12/2024`, 700 kW ac, Category 2); no co-located legacy DER (`Existing_DER_Register_Extract.xlsx`); no unpaid CWO balance or equipment waitlist hold (`Construction_WO_Payment_Ledger.xlsx`, `2025-07-14_On_Hold_Queue_Report.xlsx`, `Completed_Sites_Awaiting_Equipment.xlsx`, `SOC_PTO_Hold_Log.xlsx`); all five Vexlar `VX-140C` inverters (`VX140C-25-03311`, `VX140C-25-03312`, `VX140C-25-03315`, `VX140C-25-03318`, `VX140C-25-03320`) listed in `CEL-2025-Q2 (published 04/30/2025)` (`Inverters` row 18, UL 1741-SB) and covered by Vexlar CoC `VX-CC-25-0522 (05/22/2025)`; Witness Test `WT-0629-01` conducted and passed `07/08/2025` (`08:10 to 15:35`) under `DO-2025-0677` (`ENG-PRC-014 Rev 3 §§4.2–4.3`, signed by `M. Halbrook, P.E., Alleniom DER Field Engineering (AFE-1042)`, `S. Rennick, Commissioning, DER Program Office`, and `K. Osei, Electrical Engineer`); revenue meter `RM-0629` set and tested `07/08/2025`; DER-side protection and `T-1` effective grounding accepted `06/18/2025` (`DPS-07 §§4.3, 4.4`); City of Wrenford Certificate of Final Approval issued `07/02/2025` under Permit `WEP-25-0317` (`NFPA 70 / NEC 2023`); and all PV string, combiner, cable tray, inverter AC output, switchboard (`NEC 705.12(B)(3)(3)`), transformer (`NEC Table 450.3(A)`), grounding (`NEC 250.52(A)(4)`), and labeling calculations on `Drawings E-101, E-201, E-301 Rev C` verified compliant with `NEC 2023`.
* **Four Matters Excluded as Under Separate Review:** (1) Company RTU and POI recloser installation, configuration, and commissioning tests (`SCADA/EMS Engineering` and `Distribution Protection Engineering`); (2) POI recloser settings and protection coordination study (`Distribution Protection Engineering`); (3) site queue position (`Meera Vellanki`, weekly queue reports); and (4) system impact study and conditions (`Ivo Grantham`'s `DER Planning Group`).
